full_judgment:
MD. SIRAJUL ISLAM, J: This Rule under section 439/561 A of the Code of Criminal procedure at the instance of the informant petitioner was issued calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Tangail and accused- opposite party Nos. 1-3 to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 24.6.86 passed by the learned sessions Judge in session- case No. 126 of 1985 arising out of Nagarpur P.S. Case No. 4(3) 85 Corresponding to G. R Case No. 24(2) 85 Should not be quashed. 

 2. The informant-petitioner, sukhil kumar sarkar filed an ejahar on 27.3.85 in Nagarpur P. S. alleging inter alia that in the night following 26.3.85 some miscreants entered into their north bhita chowchala tin shed by\ cutting a sindh and Killed his father Madan Mohan Sarkar and injuried his mother on this ejahar Nagarpur p.s, Case No. 4(3) 85 corresponding to G. R; Case No, 24(2) 85 was started. Police after competing investigation submitted charge sheet on 25.7.85 against the three accused-opposite-parties under sections 450/380/ 326/302/34 of the Penal Code. The case being triable by the Court of Session was sent by the learned Magistrate to the Court of session on 22.11.85. The learned Sessions Judge, Tangail took cognizence of the case on 21.12.85 and registered it as session case no. 120 of 1985. Thereafter, the accused opposite parties filed an application on '24.6.86 in the Court of learned sessions judge praying for releasing them from the charge and for holding a further investigation of the case on the 'ground that one Asan Ali made an extrajudicial statement implicating himself and some others in the murder on this application the learned Sessions Judge passed the impugned order dated 24.6.86 directing the police for holding further investigation of the case. 

 4. Mr. Showkat Ali Khan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the informant-petitioner has submitted that the learned Sessions Judge is not justified in passing the impugned order for further investigation on the prayer of the accused persons. The learned Advocate further submits that the tape record of the so-called extra-judicial statement of one Asan Ali on the basis of which the accused-persons prayed for further investigation of the case came from their custody and that it is a fabricated pieces of paper created by the accused opposite parties and that the learned Sessions Judge has committed illegality in directing further investigation on the basis of such a piece of paper at the instance of the accused persons which has occasioned a failure of justice and as such the impugned order is liable to be set aside. 

 5. Mr. S. A. M. Mahbub Elahi, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the accused-opposite parties has, on the other hand, submitted that one Asan Ali made an extra-judicial confession before the local chairman and other respectable persons which was recorded in a Tape and was reduced in writing by the local chairman. The learned advocate submits that this Asan Ali made the extra-judicial statement implicating himself and some more persons in the murder .of Madan Mohan Sarker other than the accused-opposite parties which necessitated further investigation of the case and as such, the learned Sessions Judge had rightly allowed further investigation of the case by the impugned order. 

 6. Mr. Showkat Ali Khan then argued that the said Asan Ali was their own man and that the accused opposite parties created this statement in their bid to save themselves from the charge of murder by reopening the case in the name of further investigation and as such the impugned order for further investigation cannot stand the scrutiny of law. 

 8. It appears from the lower court Record that the accused-opposite parties were arrested on 29.5.85 and investigating officer submitted charge sheet on 25.7.85 and thereafter on 6.11.85 the accused opposite parties filed an application before the learned Magistrate praying for releasing them from the charge and for holding a further investigation alleging that the said Ahsan Ali made the Extra-judicial statement on 3.11.85, but that the learned Magistrate did not consider that application and sent the case on 27.11.85 to the Court of Sessions Judge for trial. It appears that after receiving the record in the Court of Sessions Judge there were as many as 11 orders passed in the sessions-record for decision of bail matters and for framing charge, but that the accused opposite parties did not move their previous petition for further investigation not did they file any fresh petition for further investigation during such a long period of time on the date of framing charge on 24.6.86, the accused opposite parties filed an application before the learned sessions Judge praying for holding further investigation and on that application the learned Sessions Judge passed the impugned order. 

 10. It appears that the copy of the application for further investigation as filed by the accused-opposite pasties before the learned session Judge is annexure-C. It appears from annexure-c that this prayer was made under section 156(3) Cr. P.C. But section 156(3) Cr. P. C. lays down that any Magistrate empowered under section 190 may order for an investigation of a cognizable case, Section 190 (1) stipulates the conditions under which a Magistrate may take cognizence of any offence. From a reading of section 156 together with section 160 (1), it appears that a magistrate instead of himself taking cognizence of an offence upon receiving a complaint, may send the complaint to the police for investigation by treating the complaint as a first information report and again a Magistrate instead of accepting a final report submitted to him by the police under section 173 may, either of his own accord or on receiving a Naraji petition from any affected person, direct the police to make further investigation of the case so as to collect further evidence if any warranting the sending up of the persons Mentioned in columns of the police report. Thus it appears that the petition for further investigations made by the accused persons in the instant case is a misconceived one not falling within the per-view of section 156(3) Cr, P.C. 

 11. Sub-section 2 of section 173 of the Code, however, provides that a superior officer of police may direct further investigation pending the orders of the Magistrate, but such direction can be given only where the superior police officer has been appointed under section 158 of the Code. Further investigation may also .be held under subsection (3B) of section 173 of the submission of police report under sub-sec. 1 of section 173 of the Code if the officer-in-charge of police station obtains further evidence in the matter. In any case, if the police after holding further investigation submits a charge sheet against the remaining accused or any others, that charge sheet is called supplementary charge-sheet, but not a substituted charge-sheet as prayed for by the accused-opposite parties in their application (Annexure-C) in the instant case. 

 13. The prayer as made by accused-opposite parties in their application for holding further investigation as per Annexure-'C' is nothing but an indirect way of reopening the case by making a reinvestigation in this connection a reference may he made to the case of State Vs. Abul kasem reported in 27 D.L.R. (HC) 342 wherein it has been held that "Further investigation is not the same thing as re-investigation. Re-investigation will result in cancellation of the charge sheet already submitted but such a course is not permitted by law. A charge sheet against a wrong person can be remedied by withdrawal of the case under section 494 Cr. P. C, The same view has been expressed by another Division Bench of this Court in the case of Sultan Ahmed Matbar Vs. The State and another reported in 37 D.L.R. (HC) 185. That was a case in which the accused-persons after submission of charge sheet filed an application praying for setting aside the proceeding and for holding further investigation of the case similar to that in the instant case before us, which prayer was allowed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge in a revision under section 439A Cr. P. C. against which the informant being petitioner took a revision under action 561A Cr. P.C. in this Court and their Lordships allowed the revision and set aside the impugned order of the learned Additional Sessions Judge with the following observations: - 

 "After submission of charge sheet the police cannot ask to cancel the same and reinvestigate the same case for the court can direct the police to reopen the investigation. There is no provision of law under which a charge-sheet once submitted can be cancelled" 

 14. In our opinion the principle as laid down in the above mentioned cases in exactly applicable in the facts and circumstances of the instant case before us. 

 16. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case as found above and with a view to preventing the accused-opposite parties from further tempering with the evidence of the case, we feel that their bail should be cancelled. 

 17. In the result, the Rule is made absolute and the impugned order dated 24.6.86 is set aside. The learned Magistrate is directed to send the case back to the learned Sessions Judge for trial of the accused persons as per charge sheet already submitted. The bail of the accused-opposite parties 1-3 is hereby cancelled and they are hereby directed to surrender before the learned Magistrate within 15 days from the receipt of the record by the Magistrate. Stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacate
